why.en: A Yale mathematics PhD who left a Vassar professorship to join the Navy in 1943, she programmed the Harvard Mark I and in 1952 wrote A-0, the first compiler. She then argued that business programmers should write in English words, which led through FLOW-MATIC to COBOL.
why.zh: 她是耶鲁大学数学博士，1943 年辞去瓦萨学院的教职加入海军，为哈佛 Mark I 编程，1952 年写出第一个编译器 A-0。之后她坚持让商业程序员用英语单词写程序，这条路经由 FLOW-MATIC 通向了 COBOL。

summary.en: Hopper was born in New York City, graduated from Vassar in mathematics and physics in 1928, and earned a PhD in mathematics at Yale in 1934. She taught at Vassar until 1943, when she joined the Navy reserve and was assigned to Howard Aiken's Mark I computer at Harvard. In 1949 she joined the Eckert–Mauchly Computer Corporation to work on UNIVAC I, where she built A-0 and then the English-language compiler FLOW-MATIC. She helped organize the effort that produced COBOL in 1959. Recalled to active duty in 1967, she was promoted to rear admiral in 1985 and retired in 1986 as the oldest serving officer in the US Navy; she died in 1992.
summary.zh: 霍普生于纽约，1928 年毕业于瓦萨学院数学与物理专业，1934 年获耶鲁大学数学博士学位。她在瓦萨学院任教到 1943 年，随后加入海军预备役，被派到哈佛大学霍华德·艾肯的 Mark I 计算机项目。1949 年她加入埃克特–莫奇利计算机公司，参与 UNIVAC I 的开发，在那里写出 A-0，又做出以英语为基础的编译器 FLOW-MATIC。1959 年，她参与组织了制定 COBOL 的工作。1967 年她被召回现役，1985 年晋升海军少将，1986 年以美国海军最年长现役军官的身份退役，1992 年去世。

style.en: She said she built the compiler because she always objected to doing anything over again once she had already done it.
style.zh: 她说，自己之所以做编译器，是因为她一向不愿意把做过的事再做一遍。

style.en: She handed out pieces of wire about 30 cm long, the distance an electrical signal travels in a nanosecond, to show audiences why computers had to be small.
style.zh: 她演讲时会分发约 30 厘米长的电线，那是电信号一纳秒走过的距离，用来说明计算机为什么必须做小。

style.en: She read constantly and widely. Her colleague Howard Bromberg complained that they would discuss a problem on the ride home; he would read the newspaper, and by 8 the next morning she had solved it.
style.zh: 她读书极多、极杂。同事霍华德·布朗伯格抱怨过：两人下班路上讨论一个问题，他回家看报纸，第二天早上 8 点去接她时，她已经把问题解决了。

timeline.zh: 获耶鲁大学数学博士学位。

timeline.en: Joins the US Navy reserve; assigned to the Harvard Mark I.
timeline.zh: 加入美国海军预备役，被派往哈佛 Mark I 项目。

timeline.en: Joins the Eckert–Mauchly Computer Corporation to work on UNIVAC I.
timeline.zh: 加入埃克特–莫奇利计算机公司，参与 UNIVAC I。
开发出第一个编译器 A-0。

timeline.en: Helps launch the CODASYL effort that creates COBOL.
timeline.zh: 参与发起 CODASYL，推动制定 COBOL。

timeline.zh: 以海军少将军衔退役，是当时海军最年长的现役军官。

timeline.zh: 去世，安葬于阿灵顿国家公墓。

works.title: A-0 System
works.en: The first compiler: it turned mathematical code into machine instructions, so programmers no longer had to rewrite common routines by hand.
works.zh: 第一个编译器：把数学代码翻译成机器指令，程序员不必再手工重写常用例程。

works.title: FLOW-MATIC (B-0)
works.en: The first language to use English-like statements for data processing, and the main ancestor of COBOL.
works.zh: 第一个用类英语语句做数据处理的语言，是 COBOL 的主要前身。

quotes.text: I've always objected to doing anything over again if I had already done it once. That was building the compiler.
quotes.zh: 我一向反对把做过一次的事情再做一遍。编译器就是这么来的。
quotes.source: Oral history interview by Angeline Pantages, Computer History Museum, 1980

lessons.en: Hopper insisted programs should be written in words the users understood, and explained abstract ideas like a nanosecond with a piece of wire.
lessons.zh: 霍普坚持程序应该用使用者看得懂的词来写，还用一截电线去解释“纳秒”这样抽象的概念。

lessons.en: Hopper noticed she kept rewriting the same routines by hand, and instead of tolerating it she built a program to do the rewriting: the compiler.
lessons.zh: 霍普发现自己总在手工重写同样的例程，她没有忍着，而是写了一个程序来替她重写，这就是编译器。
